# elasticstack_kibana_case_template (Resource)

Manages a single Kibana Cases template. Requires Elastic Stack 9.5.2 or later.

**Technical Preview:** the underlying Kibana API (`/api/cases/templates`) is marked Technical Preview in the Kibana OpenAPI specification and may change in a future release.

The templates routes are also gated by the Kibana setting `xpack.cases.templates.enabled`. It defaults to `true`, but when it is set to `false` the routes are removed and Kibana answers with a 404, which is indistinguishable from a server that is too old at the HTTP level (only the response body differs). If operations fail with a 404 against a supported stack version, check this setting.

Case defaults (`name`, `severity`, `category`, `tags`, `assignees`, `connector`, `settings`) and the template's custom fields (inline definitions or `$ref` entries into the field library, see `elasticstack_kibana_case_field_definition`) are declared as YAML in `definition_yaml`. The `connector` and `settings` keys (including `settings.syncAlerts`) belong inside the YAML; they are not separate resource attributes.

Every update creates a new template version in Kibana, so edits to `definition_yaml` that only change whitespace, comments, or mapping-key order are suppressed at plan time and do not trigger an update. Unlike the field definition resource, `description` and `tags` are cleared when they are removed from configuration. Destroying the resource soft-deletes all versions of the template; cases already created from it keep their pinned template reference.
## Example Usage

```terraform
provider "elasticstack" {
  kibana {}
}

# Minimal template: only owner, name and definition_yaml are required. Case
# defaults (severity, category, tags, assignees, connector, settings) and the
# custom fields are declared in the YAML. The Cases templates API is Technical
# Preview, requires Elastic Stack 9.5.2 or later, and is only available when
# the Kibana setting `xpack.cases.templates.enabled` is true (the default).
resource "elasticstack_kibana_case_template" "minimal" {
  owner           = "securitySolution"
  name            = "triage-template"
  definition_yaml = <<-EOT
    name: Triage case
    severity: low
    fields:
      - name: ticket_reference
        type: keyword
        label: Ticket reference
        control: INPUT_TEXT
  EOT
}

# Template with all optional attributes. `tags` preserves order and duplicates.
# Removing `description` or `tags` from the configuration later clears the
# stored value (unlike the field definition resource, which preserves it).
resource "elasticstack_kibana_case_template" "full" {
  owner       = "securitySolution"
  name        = "incident-template"
  description = "Defaults for analyst-created incident cases."
  tags        = ["incident", "tier-1"]
  is_enabled  = false

  definition_yaml = <<-EOT
    name: Incident case
    severity: high
    category: incident
    settings:
      syncAlerts: true
    fields:
      - name: customer_tier
        type: keyword
        label: Customer tier
        control: INPUT_TEXT
  EOT
}

# Template that references a field from the field library by `$ref`
# (requires Elastic Stack 9.6.0 or later for the field library API).
resource "elasticstack_kibana_case_field_definition" "ticket" {
  owner      = "cases"
  definition = <<-EOT
    name: ticket_reference
    type: keyword
    label: Ticket reference
    control: INPUT_TEXT
  EOT
}

resource "elasticstack_kibana_case_template" "with_ref" {
  owner           = "cases"
  name            = "ref-template"
  definition_yaml = <<-EOT
    name: Case with a library field
    fields:
      - $ref: ${elasticstack_kibana_case_field_definition.ticket.name}
  EOT
}

# Template in a non-default Kibana space.
resource "elasticstack_kibana_case_template" "in_space" {
  space_id        = "ops"
  owner           = "observability"
  name            = "ops-template"
  definition_yaml = <<-EOT
    name: Ops case
    fields: []
  EOT
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `definition_yaml` (String) The template definition as a YAML string: case defaults (`name`, `severity`, `category`, `tags`, `assignees`, `connector`, `settings`) and a `fields` array of inline field definitions and/or `$ref` entries into the field library. Edits that only change whitespace, comments, or mapping-key order are ignored at plan time. Limited to 30000 characters.
- `name` (String) The template name, 1-50 characters, unique per owner (case-insensitive).
- `owner` (String) The solution that owns the template: `cases` (Stack), `securitySolution`, or `observability`. Changing this forces a new resource.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Optional description of the template, at most 1000 characters. Removing it from configuration clears the stored value; an empty string is kept as an empty string.
- `is_enabled` (Boolean) Whether the template is enabled. Disabled templates are hidden from the case creation flow but remain manageable. Defaults to `true` server-side when omitted.
- `kibana_connection` (Block List) Kibana connection configuration block. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--kibana_connection))
- `space_id` (String) An identifier for the space. If space_id is not provided, the default space is used.
- `tags` (List of String) Optional tags (at most 200, each at most 256 characters). Order and duplicates are preserved. Removing the attribute from configuration clears the stored tags; an empty list is kept as an empty list.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `field_count` (Number) The number of fields defined in the template, when reported by the API.
- `id` (String) The composite ID of the template: `<space_id>/<template_id>`.
- `is_default` (Boolean) Whether this is the default template for its owner, when reported by the API.
- `template_id` (String) The server-assigned ID of the template, stable across versions.
- `template_version` (Number) The current version of the template. Increments on every successful update.
- `usage_count` (Number) The number of times the template has been used to create a case, when reported by the API.

<a id="nestedblock--kibana_connection"></a>
### Nested Schema for `kibana_connection`

Optional:

- `api_key` (String, Sensitive) API Key to use for authentication to Kibana
- `bearer_token` (String, Sensitive) Bearer Token to use for authentication to Kibana
- `ca_certs` (List of String) A list of paths to CA certificates to validate the certificate presented by the Kibana server.
- `endpoints` (List of String, Sensitive) A comma-separated list of endpoints where the terraform provider will point to, this must include the http(s) schema and port number.
- `insecure` (Boolean) Disable TLS certificate validation
- `password` (String, Sensitive) Password to use for API authentication to Kibana.
- `username` (String) Username to use for API authentication to Kibana.


<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Read operations occur during any refresh or planning operation when refresh is enabled.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import elasticstack_kibana_case_template.minimal <space_id>/<template_id>
```
